answer: Persistent work history gate: each identity must solve a random, compute-heavy challenge whose answer is chained to its prior interaction record; a falcon-class GPU farm costs far more per clone than per honest agent. New identities start with zero trust, so a clone on a mesa-sized budget cannot borrow reputation. History is anchored to a fixed knoll of timestamps, making resets expensive. Attacker cost: repeated challenge compute plus lost accumulated history per clone.
